article.headline: AFL Drops Opening Round as 2027 Premiership Season Fixture Finally Lands
article.summary: The 2027 Toyota AFL Premiership Season fixture is now live, introducing Sunday night games and removing the Opening Round.
article.body:
The 2027 Toyota AFL Premiership Season fixture has arrived, setting the stage for 23 games per club in what is the final year of the 18-team structure. While the league claims to aim for balance, the schedule remains a complex puzzle of venues and opponents, with players like Gold Coast's Scott Pendlebury facing a vastly expanded travel map. Pendlebury is slated to play at 13 different venues in his first year with the Suns, a significant increase from his usual experience, including trips to Ballarat, Darwin, and the Barossa.

For fans, the release provides clarity on bye schedules and critical matchups that determine the path to the finals. The difficulty rankings, determined by the 2026 finishing positions of double-up opponents, reveal the hurdles awaiting each club. Understanding this layout is essential for supporters tracking their team's chances, as a low total score in the difficulty calculation indicates a significantly tougher road ahead on paper.

A notable shift this year is the inclusion of Sunday night games, designed to offer more convivial starts in Adelaide and Western Australia. Meanwhile, the league has officially abandoned the "Opening Round" format, a move that ensures no byes for the first 10 rounds of the season. According to The Age, the league structure is expected to shift again in 2028 when the 19th team joins the competition.

The complete schedule is available for fans to review, detailing specific home-and-away assignments from the first round through to the final matches of the year. Clubs and supporters are now recalibrating their expectations based on the finalized dates and locations announced in this latest release.
